transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rory Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Desai (Aurelia Head of ML), Priya Natarajan (Eng Mgr), Luis Ortega (SRE), Dana Kim (Product), Jorge Alvarez (Data Scientist)

Summary:
Quick sync to decide which model variant to 'anchor' (pin) for the next pilot week, agree emergency unpin/escape-hatch steps, and finalize what metrics we gather during the anchor run. Short tech deep dive on failure modes and SLOs.

Topics:
- model anchor (pin) candidate selection and rationale
- rollback/emergency-unpin runbook and triggers
- telemetry needed: latency, token costs, hallucination/regression signals
- private vs hosted routing for the anchored run

Referenced artifacts:
- Pin matrix draft: https://redwood.app/notes/pin-matrix-aurelia-03-11 (shared)
- Benchmark script repo: https://git.aurelia/poctests/anchor-bench (shared)
- Security summary (SOC2 excerpt) link posted in chat

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Okay, thanks all for jumping on. We're on the agenda to pick an anchor model for the pilot week and to hash out emergency unpin. Samir, do you want to open with where you landed after the eval runs?
[00:18] Samir: Yeah, sure thanks. Uh so we ran the three top candidates, the open-llm-1-12b-ish, the redwood-compat-flavored 7B quant, and the fanti (or - I think it said 'Fathom') 13B variant — the numbers are a bit noisy but throughput wise the 7B quant wins for our 200ms median latency goal. Quality-wise the 13B had fewer NER regressions on the forms data.
[00:42] Priya: And what's the cost delta? We need to justify the pick to finance if we pick the 13B.
[00:50] Jorge: Roughly 2.4x token cost on our current batch distribution when using the 13B vs the 7B quant, but we saw a 12% reduction in hallucination-like scoring on our prompt-set.
[01:12] Rory: Right, so tradeoff is cost vs quality. One option is anchor the cheaper 7B quant and shadow the 13B to collect quality signals and only fail over if we detect a regression above threshold. That keeps economics good but gives you a safety path.
[01:34] Dana: When you say 'fail over' — what does that look like in practice? Is it a regional swap, or full traffic cutover?
[01:40] Rory: Can be either. For this pilot we recommend a soft-fallback: route a small percentage to 13B (shadow or canary) and have an automated policy that routes more if quality drops on the primary. Emergency unpin would be manual — an SRE step to unpin and route to a pre-approved model variant.
[02:05] Luis: We need the checklist for emergency unpin. Our compliance folks want explicit KMS change windows and audit log steps so we can track key rotation if we switch to a private model variant.
[02:19] Maya: Totally. We'll put those items into the runbook. Quick note — some of the product names in the slides might be auto-transcribed wrong; the 'K-V cash' reference is KV cache. Sorry about that.
[02:36] Samir: Haha, no problem.
[02:40] Priya: Can we get a clear SLA on the pin duration? Like, we commit to anchor for X days before we allow re-evaluation?
[02:48] Maya: We usually recommend a minimum 7-day anchor to collect meaningful regression signals, but we can shorten with stricter monitoring. For this pilot, 7 days sounds reasonable unless you want a 72h burn-in.
[03:05] Samir: Let's do 7 days. We need time to evaluate user-edge regressions.
[03:12] Rory: Cool. On triggers — propose three tiers: (1) automated metric trigger (e.g., 5% increase in top-line failure rate / hallucination score over baseline for 1 hour), (2) operator alert (on-call SRE observes degradation), (3) manual Product override for safety-critical UX issues.
[03:34] Jorge: On the hallucination metric — our detector is noisy. We saw spikes that were false positives. How do we avoid flip-flopping?
[03:40] Rory: Good point. You need smoothing and a debounce window, like a 60-minute rolling average and confirm with a small human-in-the-loop sample before escalating to emergency unpin.
[03:51] Priya: Is there an automated 'rollback' command in Redwood Console or is that all API driven?
[03:58] Maya: Both. There's a one-click rollback in the Console for standard hosted flows — that executes the model routing policy change. For Private deployments we push an API call plus an orchestration playbook so you can integrate with your runbooks.
[04:13] Luis: For Private we also need the Ops-side SSH and KMS notes. If we unpin to an on-prem variant there's a key import step, and we need to record that for SOC2.
[04:26] Maya: We'll include sample KMS import steps and audit log snippets in the runbook.
[04:33] Samir: Another question: tokenization mismatches caused one of our scoring metrics to spike last week — how do we control for tokenizer differences across variants?
[04:42] Rory: We recommend normalizing by using the same tokenizer package in your client instrumentation or run synthetic traces through both tokenizers to build a token-length mapping table. We'll send a script to do that.
[04:56] Jorge: That'd help.
[05:00] Dana: On the routing policy, can we pin by request attribute? Like, we have an enterprise tenant where we want stricter quality — can we keep them on 13B while everyone else is on 7B?
[05:09] Rory: Yes, targeting by route/tenant is supported — and you can set different pins per route. We'll show a sample config in the pin matrix.
[05:19] Maya: Quick demo — Rory, you wanna pull up the pin matrix?
[05:22] Rory: Sure, sharing screen... (brief pause) Alright, the matrix lists candidate model id, reason to anchor, expected latency, cost multiplier, suggested fallback and a 'confidence' column. For Aurelia we marked 7b-quant as 'anchor candidate A' and 13b-fathom as 'fallback-high-quality'. There's also a 'shadow' column we recommend to enable for first 72 hours.
[06:00] Priya: In the confidence column I see '0.6' next to 7B — what does that represent?
[06:04] Rory: It's a subjective confidence score from the bench runs — 0.6 means decent results but not ironclad. We included notes on dataset mismatch and some failure modes observed on long conversations.
[06:20] Samir: One failure mode was KV cache thrash on conversation context longer than 1k tokens — the 13B handled it better. Might be because of different attention implementations.
[06:33] Rory: Right and that aligns with our kernel selection note — larger models sometimes pick different caching strategies. We'll annotate which models have known cache/attn caveats.
[06:45] Maya: On the topic of quantization: your 7B is a 4-bit quant variant — if you see subtle semantic drift we'll recommend a small bias correction via prompt tuning rather than immediate unpin.
[07:00] Jorge: Prompt tuning is cheap but it's extra ops. Do we have metrics on how much prompt-tune reduces hallucination on the 7B?
[07:08] Rory: Early numbers show small improvements, like 4-6% reduction for the forms set, not as much as moving to 13B though. It's a tool in the toolbox.
[07:21] Priya: Okay, so plan proposal: anchor 7B quant, enable shadowing to 13B at 10% for first 72 hours, collect telemetry, then review at day 7. Emergency unpin runbook with operator steps + KMS checklist. Agree?
[07:36] Samir: Sounds good. Two caveats — (1) we need to make sure the 7B has deterministic tokenizers across nodes, and (2) confirm we can do the shadowing without doubling quota costs.
[07:48] Maya: On quota: shadowing will only add inference costs for the shadowed requests but we can limit sampling rate. We'll send an estimate for 10% shadowing cost.
[08:00] Luis: For the unpin checklist, include: who is authorized (names/emails), who has KMS rotate permissions, what audit tags to add, and how to rollback the rollback if needed. We've seen double rollbacks confuse downstream logs.
[08:18] Rory: Good call — include a 'deadman's switch' note: after an emergency unpin, block automatic re-pin for 24h without a manual approval.
[08:29] Dana: That would prevent oscillation.
[08:32] Priya: On alerts — can Redwood emit a pre-baked alert for 'model-quality-regression' with sample traces attached to Slack?
[08:40] Maya: Yes, you can wire alerts into Slack/email and include a trace link. We'll provide an example alert rule.
[08:48] Jorge: Any gotchas with embeddings or reranking flows when we switch models? We use a reranker downstream.
[08:55] Rory: Reranker compatibility is something to test. If reranker is embedding based, you might need to reindex or run a consistency check. We'll add a reranker checklist item.
[09:06] Samir: For the anchor run, our immediate measurement plan is: latency p50/p95, token cost, hallucination score, regression on 50-item human-labeled prompt set, and production error rate. Anything else?
[09:18] Maya: Also include tokenization mismatch map and a small sample of KV cache hit/miss ratios.
[09:24] Priya: Who's responsible for the human-labeled review?
[09:28] Samir: Jorge and his team will do the first pass; if unclear we'll escalate to Product for judgment.
[09:34] Maya: Alright — I have 4 quick asks to close out: we'll send the annotated pin matrix and the runbook, Rory will share the benchmark script and tokenizer normalization script, Samir runs the 48h anchored run and uploads traces, and Luis drafts the emergency unpin checklist.
[09:51] Samir: Got it.
[09:53] Luis: Yep.
[09:55] Dana: One last question — what's the recommended rollback cadence if we see continuous small regressions? Do we wait for the 7 days?
[10:03] Rory: If it's severe — don't wait. Use the emergency unpin. If it's small and trending, we'll monitor and consider a quick fix like prompt nudge or temporary route adjustments. The 7-day is for evaluation not a hard lock when safety is impacted.
[10:18] Priya: Makes sense.
[10:20] Maya: Okay I'll recap in the follow-up email and attach the artifacts. Any other blockers?
[10:26] (brief silence)
[10:30] Jorge: One tiny nit, in your matrix you had a model id spelled 'rwdw-13b' — please confirm the exact model id for the fallback so we don't misconfigure the routing.
[10:38] Rory: We'll confirm exact model ids in the pin matrix CSV.
[10:41] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the 48-hour run results and schedule the tabletop drill.
[10:48] Samir: Thanks all.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: some product names may be slightly mistranscribed (e.g., 'K-V cash' -> KV cache, 'Fathom' model label uncertain). There was occasional crosstalk and truncated sentences.
